thread:
Priya (support): @Hannah urgent ticket from customer 'MedStream' — they report a 30m window of 502 + 504s when calling /v1/generate. Said it broke their live inference; attached x-request-ids and two curl outputs.

Hannah (oncall): Thanks. I'm seeing an alert from alertmanager: generate-api: 5xx-rate > 0.6% for 10m. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/generate-api-overview . Can someone paste a sampling of x-request-ids?

Priya (support): sample x-request-ids: req_20261203_a3f4, req_20261203_a40b, req_20261203_a5d2. Customer logs show 502 "bad gateway" and one 504 with nginx timeout.

Lukas (SRE): running quick Loki query for upstream errors: `{app="edge-proxy"} |= "upstream" | json |~ "5.."` — spike at 2026-12-03T19:12Z. Also noticed a cluster of TLS alert logs: "SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to backend" toward model-pool-b.

tracing-bot: trace sample for req_20261203_a3f4 -> root span edge-proxy, downstream span router-service present, but missing model-host span (gap). Trace sampling rate default is 2% so gaps are expected, but many errors coincide with dropped child spans.

Hannah (oncall): hypothesis: intermittent TLS failure between router and model hosts causing connection resets; the edge times out waiting and replies 502/504. Could also be sudden CPU contention on model nodes causing slow accepts. Diego — any recent infra changes?

Diego (platform): we bumped openssl on model-hosts last week and rotated certs for pool-b yesterday at 03:00Z. No rolling restarts scheduled near 19:10Z. I see health checks flapping for model-pool-b around 19:11Z though. Pushing healthcheck logs.

Lukas (SRE): runbook repro steps for support/eng diagnostics: 1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"inputs":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --max-time 45 -I 2) include response headers and X-Request-ID 3) if you see TLS errors, run `openssl s_client -connect <model-host>:443 -tls1_3` from router pods to verify handshake.

Priya (support): told customer to re-run with --max-time 45 and send any x-request-ids. They sent three more; two succeeded after 30s, one failed with 502.

Lukas (SRE): digging deeper: nginx upstream logs show a pattern: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and occasionally `110: Connection timed out`. Also noticed a small but sharp increase in retry attempts from the router (5xx retry logic kicking in). Query in Loki:
```
{job="router"} |= "upstream prematurely closed" | count_over_time(15m)
```
shows a 6x jump at 19:10-19:15Z.

Diego (platform): scaling notes: model-pool-b had 12 pods pre-incident. Autoscaler tried to add 3 pods but kube API had transient 429s due to a control-plane rate limit at 19:13Z. So scale didn't finish before errors spiked. I'm increasing replica quota and retry windows.

Hannah (oncall): mitigation applied: temporarily route heavy customers away from model-pool-b using traffic-split rule (applied at 19:25Z). Also increased proxy_read_timeout in edge-proxy from 30s to 60s for the duration.

loki-bot: metric update: 5xx rate dropped from 0.85% -> 0.18% within 5m after routing change. Some customers still see intermittent timeouts.

Priya (support): MedStream confirmed fewer errors after 19:30Z but noted higher latency on some requests (~2x). They asked if there's a permanent fix.

Lukas (SRE): follow-ups: 1) Investigate TLS handshake flakiness on model-pool-b: collect openssl error codes and kernel logs from hosts. 2) Increase router->model_trace sampling to 10% during incidents so we capture child spans more reliably. 3) Add Grafana panel for `upstream prematurely closed` and control-plane 429 correlation.

Diego (platform): also action: revert the cert rotation on pool-b (we have a backup cert) and run a canary validation before mass rotate. Will also add jitter/retry to scale operations to avoid control-plane bursts.

Hannah (oncall): runbook update tasks: add explicit step to check control-plane 429s when autoscaling fails, and a quick reroute command to avoid impacted pools. I'll file a docs PR.

Priya (support): will send an executive summary to MedStream and link to postmortem when ready. Provided workaround steps (longer timeout, retry with exponential backoff).

Lukas (SRE): one last note — we should treat TLS handshake failures as a first-class signal in our alerting (currently masked as 502). Propose a new alert: `router.tls.handshake.failures > 5/min` to trigger earlier.

Hannah (oncall): agreed. I'll create the incident page and owner tags. Lukas, Diego — can one of you take postmortem write-up? I'll own the runbook updates.

Diego (platform): I'll start the postmortem draft and attach the control-plane and cert-rotation timelines.

Lukas (SRE): I'll add trace sampling change and the Grafana panel. Marking thread resolved for now.

Priya (support): closing loop with MedStream; they appreciate the quick action. Will reopen if they see new 5xx clusters. :thumbsup:

Hannah (oncall): monitoring: alertmanager will keep watching 5xx rate for 2 hours; re-open if >0.4% sustained for 5m. Thanks team."
